Bug_Title: BSHIFT: 32 bit int shifted by an amount not in the range -31..31 (ICAST_BAD_SHIFT_AMOUNT)
Bug_Details:
The code performs shift of a 32 bit int by a constant amount outside
the range -31..31.
The effect of this is to use the lower 5 bits of the integer
value to decide how much to shift by (e.g., shifting by 40 bits is the same as shifting by 8 bits,
and shifting by 32 bits is the same as shifting by zero bits). This probably isn't what was expected,
and it is at least confusing.
Bug_Explanation: The code performs a left shift operation on a 32-bit integer by a constant amount outside the range of -31 to 31. This is a common bug where the lower 5 bits of the integer are used to decide the shift amount, which is likely not the intended behavior and can lead to confusion.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case 'testShowBugWithInvalidShiftAmount' triggers the bug by passing a shift amount of 32 to the'showBug' method, which is outside the valid range of -31 to 31. This causes the '<<' operator to use the lower 5 bits of the shift amount, which is likely not the intended behavior.
